surface_layman.summary: In Generation 4b, we moved away from one giant compiler that does everything. When one AI tries to do research, code, test, and judge its own work, it inevitably hallucinates or cuts corners. Instead, Generation 4b breaks the workload into 5 sovereign services running on isolated private networks. They communicate via an automated protocol bus, keeping each other honest.

key_benefits.title: Zero-Trust Separation of Concerns
key_benefits.desc: The AI that writes the code is physically barred from doing research or grading its own tests.

key_benefits.title: Automated Math Mediation
key_benefits.desc: When the builder hits a friction point, it doesn't improvise; an automated math engine verifies if a proposed tweak preserves invariants.

key_benefits.title: Tamper-Proof Flight Recorder
key_benefits.desc: Every single communication, token spend, and test witness is hashed into a cryptographic Merkle-DAG.

key_benefits.title: Human Driver's Seat
key_benefits.desc: Operators retain an instant 1-click emergency brake, negative veto power (NEG-###), and 1-tap state rollback capability.

asymmetric_rfc_bus.title: Asymmetric RFC Protocol Bus
asymmetric_rfc_bus.layman: When the Builder encounters an obstacle (e.g., token limits or a contradictory rule), it cannot guess or hallucinate. Instead, it files a formal 'Request for Adjustment'. The Research Service and an automated math solver (Z3 SMT Prover) evaluate the request. If the adjustment breaks a safety invariant, it is rejected with a mathematical proof. If safe, an approved amendment is signed.
